natural_language: Two strictly positive parameters are given, named first and second. A real-valued random variable Z is normally distributed. Its location is second and its scale is first — the reverse of the reference form. Both assignments type-check, because both parameters are strictly positive, so nothing but the role labels distinguishes them.

expected_semantics.relation_to_reference: different meaning; must NOT share a canonical hash

distractors: Judging this equivalent to the reference because the same two symbols appear in the same distribution. Role assignment is the meaning.
Expecting the type checker to catch the swap. It cannot: both are PositiveReal, and a PositiveReal is a valid location. Only the role label carries the difference.
